audit.whatIsWrong: diff HARD at 8/10 and report[14] quoting 37.8%, against a packet win rate of 57.65% over 196 games. The packet flags the chart itself (Olaf 6 stages to 1).
audit.why: The page tells the player this is one of his worst lanes while the data says he wins it comfortably.
audit.corrected: diff EVEN, 5/10, tone recoloured, both prose statements restated at 57.65%, and the first-item stage moved to Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: Row 5 (First item) gave Olaf the stage in both layers.
audit.why: Kraken/BORK is Yi's flip point and the packet chart contradiction has to be resolved somewhere; the first-item row is the one the rest of the page already describes as close.
audit.corrected: phases[5].side and win[5] flipped to Skill as a matched pair, with the rating and why updated.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer credits Olaf with 'Vicious Strikes' as a lifesteal ability. Olaf's W is Tough It Out — attack speed and a shield, no lifesteal. The lifesteal is on his passive, Berserker Rage, and scales with his MISSING health. The layer also credits Alpha Strike with true damage; Alpha Strike is physical, Wuju Style (E) is the true damage. Ragnarok was described as granting move speed; Riot's text grants disable immunity while attacking plus passive armour and MR.
audit.why: Three separate wrong facts that change play: you cannot cut lifesteal by baiting a W that has none, you cannot rely on Q for true damage, and you wait out Ragnarok by staying away, not by outrunning a speed buff he does not get.
audit.corrected: Every 'Vicious Strikes' replaced with Berserker Rage and the missing-health scaling stated; true damage reattributed to Wuju Style; Ragnarok restated as disable immunity plus free resists, with its 100/90/80 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Undertow's reset was never stated: picking the axe back up refunds the whole cooldown.
audit.why: It means 'his Q is down' is only true if he did not walk over the axe — the single most-missed timing in the lane.
audit.corrected: spikes[0] and early now state the 9s cooldown and the pickup reset.
sources: enemyKit Q 'If Olaf picks up the axe, the ability's cooldown is reset'

edits.before: His first bruiser item (Black Cleaver/Trinity) plus lifesteal still beats your Kraken/BORK first item in a straight duel since his true damage ignores any armor or defensive piece you bought.
edits.after: His first bruiser item plus Berserker Rage's lifesteal matches your Kraken/BORK, so the duel turns on whether you space his Undertow and refuse to fight inside the Ragnarok window.

edits.before: Reckless Swing true damage and Vicious Strikes keep every early trade his.
edits.after: Reckless Swing true damage and Tough It Out's shield keep early trades his.

edits.before: Ragnarok's CC immunity and speed make his level-6 all-in unbeatable for you.
edits.after: Ragnarok's disable immunity and free resists make his 6 all-in unbeatable.

edits.before: At two items Highlander and Alpha Strike true damage finally out-burst his healing.
edits.after: At two items Highlander and Wuju Style true damage out-race his lifesteal now.

edits.before: Olaf is one of Yi's worst early matchups: Undertow axe slows you, his Vicious Strikes lifesteal outsustains your trades, and Reckless Swing deals true damage that Meditate can't fully mitigate, so avoid all trades.
edits.after: Olaf is one of Yi's worst early matchups: Undertow slows you and its 9s cooldown resets the moment he picks the axe up, Berserker Rage feeds him attack speed and lifesteal as he drops low, and Reckless Swing is true damage Meditate cannot mitigate.

edits.before: Ragnarok makes Olaf immune to all your crowd control and gives him move speed to stick to you, and his low-health attack speed lets him beat you straight up, so do not fight him even with Highlander up.
edits.after: Ragnarok makes Olaf immune to disables for as long as he keeps attacking and passively hands him armour and MR, so Highlander will not save you — at 100s rank 1 it is the one cooldown worth waiting out.

edits.before: Only at full crit and on-hit items do you flip: Highlander plus Alpha Strike true-damage bursts him faster than his lifesteal can heal, and you can finally win the extended fight he used to dominate.
edits.after: Only at two-plus on-hit items do you flip: Wuju Style's true damage ignores the resists Ragnarok hands him and out-races Berserker Rage's lifesteal, so the extended fight he used to own becomes yours.

edits.before: Olaf shuts you down early — his Undertow slow lets him engage on your terms, Vicious Strikes outsustains you, and Reckless Swing true damage chunks a squishy Yi through Meditate, so play for farm and nothing else.
edits.after: Olaf shuts you down early — Undertow slows on a 9s cooldown that resets the instant he walks over the axe, and Reckless Swing is true damage costing him health, which only feeds Berserker Rage's lifesteal. Farm, nothing else.

edits.before: He keeps the lead all the way to your first item: Ragnarok at 6 makes him CC-immune and faster, so you can't kite or all-in him, and his low-health attack speed wins any straight duel.
edits.after: He holds the lead to your first item: Ragnarok at 6 makes him immune to disables while he keeps attacking, and Berserker Rage's low-health attack speed wins any straight duel.

edits.before: The matchup finally flips at two-plus items — Highlander and Alpha Strike true damage let you out-burst his lifesteal, and you can win the extended fight, but only once you've fully scaled past his early dominance.
edits.after: The matchup flips at two-plus items — Highlander plus Wuju Style true damage out-races his lifesteal and ignores the resists Ragnarok grants, so you win the extended fight, but only once you have fully scaled.

edits.before: Sustain through trades with Vicious Strikes and Reckless Swing true damage
edits.after: Sustain through trades with Berserker Rage lifesteal and true damage

edits.before: It's an 8/10 because Olaf attacks all three of your weaknesses at once: he has a slow to stop you kiting, true damage that ignores your only defensive tools, and a Ragnarok window that hard-counters Alpha Strike and Highlander — your two escape/chase buttons — exactly when you're weakest.
edits.after: It's a 5/10 and you take it 57.65%: Olaf attacks three weaknesses at once — a slow to stop you kiting, true damage that ignores your defensive tools, and a Ragnarok window that beats Alpha Strike and Highlander — but all of that lands before your items, and none of it survives them.

edits.before: Olaf owns levels 1 through 6 — his hardest spike is level 6 Ragnarok — and only at your two-plus-item window does favor finally tip to you, and only in a properly spaced fight.
edits.after: Olaf owns levels 1 through 5 — his hardest spike is level 6 Ragnarok — it levels out at your first item and tips to you at two-plus items, in a properly spaced fight.

edits.before: HARD (37.8% WR, 8/10 difficulty): Olaf counters every Yi weakness at once — slow, true damage, and a CC-immune Ragnarok that beats Alpha Strike and Highlander — so play to survive and scale, not to win the lane.
edits.after: EVEN (57.65% WR, 5/10 difficulty): Olaf counters every Yi weakness at once — slow, true damage, and a Ragnarok that ignores disables — but your two-item on-hit reclaims it, so play to survive and scale.

notes: Olaf's W in the kit file is Tough It Out (attack speed + shield). The content layer's 'Vicious Strikes' is a dead ability name and it was also attached to lifesteal that actually lives on the passive — that is the biggest single error I found on this champion so far. Undertow carries a 'grounding' derived flag but Riot's text describes only armour and move-speed reduction, so I wrote no grounding claim.
